proofs.text: In a temp git project with `greeting.py`, one spec holding a medium-risk rule and one tagged test, run init at `passed` and verify the quick run exits 0, that `--record --commit` writes a record under `.purlin/records/greeting/` and the gate check exits 0. Raise to `strong` and verify the gate check exits 1; commit a second record under the build identity, verify it is labelled `ci` and the gate check exits 0. Raise to `signed` and verify the gate check exits 1 naming `purlin:init --gate signed`; set one signer and verify it exits 1 again; write a signature and verify the commit is signed and the gate check exits 0. Walk both the python and the typescript fixture

rule_text: A project init set up walks the three gates: the quick run passes, a record the developer commits meets `passed`, raising to `strong` refuses that record and accepts one the build identity committed, and `signed` refuses first an empty signer list and then a rule at or above `sign_at` with no signature, until a signature is written in a signed commit

tests.name: the three gates walked on every fixture init set up
